answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: every caller and every answerer hold a checkout of the same two roots (cairn, CairnCommons), possibly at different absolute paths — true on every fleet box (akienasus ~/cairn, Dell ~/dev/src/cairn, akiendell C:\automation\local\cairn). On akienasus the cairn checkout and the commons are not siblings, which is why _roots() takes cairn from the module's own location and the commons from edges.commons_root (CAIRN_ROOTS_PARENT honoured). A path outside both roots (a scratch HOME, /tmp) cannot cross by root; it raises, which may red a judge call that today passes a tmp path between two processes on ONE box: the builder runs every proof using ask() and reports any that sends a tmp path.
answers.builder_check: A builder needs: where the roots come from (named: module parents[3] and edges.commons_root), what happens to a path outside them (raise, then report any proof it breaks), and how to make caller and answerer differ in one process (monkeypatch _roots per side; for clause 2, launch codemother with CAIRN_ROOTS_PARENT pointing at a scratch copy). All are in the ticket's how.

answers.falsifier_check: Four clauses: the path rebuilds under the answerer's root; /sorted's path referent is judged True across differing roots; an unplaceable path raises at either end; a backslash rel decodes on Linux. Horizon: until the wire gains a third root or judges stop taking Paths.
